title: Shipwrecks: ancient cargoes and maritime graveyards
subtitle: Losses through 1934, accumulating across coasts and lakes
description: Explore early excavated cargoes, named disasters and regional concentrations of historical losses.

scenes.title: Dokos — Early Helladic cargo assemblage
scenes.body: Pottery concentrated in Skindos Bay is interpreted by the excavators as a lost ship’s cargo. It is among the earliest excavated maritime-loss assemblages.
scenes.note: No preserved ship hull establishes its outline. The approximate date and rounded bay-level marker do not identify a sinking day or a surveyed wreck footprint.

scenes.title: Uluburun — copper, tin and luxury cargo
scenes.body: Copper and tin ingots, glass, pottery and luxury materials reveal a wide Late Bronze Age maritime network. Hull fragments preserve pegged mortise-and-tenon construction.
scenes.note: Cargo origins do not prove every port visited, the ship’s intended destination or a continuous mapped itinerary.

scenes.title: Cape Gelidonya — metalworking cargo
scenes.body: A merchant vessel lost near the cape carried metal ingots, scrap and tools. The assemblage shows how maritime movement supplied metalworking.
scenes.note: The point locates the cape and adjacent islands approximately. Tools suggest onboard metalworking; they do not identify a named crew.

scenes.title: Kyrenia — a Hellenistic merchant ship
scenes.body: A surviving wooden hull and cargo off northern Cyprus document a Hellenistic merchant vessel. Almonds and newly cleaned wood samples help constrain its final voyage.
scenes.note: This is a probability interval, not 25 years of repeated wrecking. The rounded offshore marker is not the museum location or an excavation plan.

method: Publisher loss dates are distinct from discovery, survey and salvage dates. Undated losses are held outside the timeline. A bright loss fades over 25 years to a persistent subtle marker; this is a visual convention, not a claim that wreckage survives. Catalogue aliases share a marker. Coverage follows the linked public inventories and is not a worldwide census.
dateNote: Only losses with a supported date or archaeological interval enter the movie. A year within an interval is not an exact sinking date. Modern relief and coastlines are reference geography.
